answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy should charge each new identity a small refundable stake that is slashed when peers flag fraud — cheap for one honest sparrow, ruinous for a thousand fake ones. Reputation then accrues slowly, like cargo arriving at a wharf: a newcomer can only dock small jobs until a history of completed work vouches for it. Finally, each agent periodically publishes a signed sonnet of its recent actions — a public, auditable log peers can verify — so duplicated personas surface before they can drain the market.
